section: Andhra Pradesh - cropping pattern, major crops, horticulture, aquaculture and fisheries

accepted.s: With reference to the position of Andhra Pradesh in the production and productivity of horticultural crops, which one of the following is correct?
o: Andhra Pradesh ranks second in productivity of papaya, cocoa and tomato
Andhra Pradesh ranks first in productivity of oil palm, papaya, lime, cocoa, tomato and chillies
Andhra Pradesh ranks first in productivity of mango, sweet orange and turmeric
Andhra Pradesh ranks second in productivity of oil palm and first in mango production
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh ranks first in productivity of oil palm, papaya, lime, cocoa, tomato and chillies. It ranks second in mango, sweet orange and turmeric.
accepted.tq: Use the comparison table to separate first-rank productivity crops from second-rank crops.
accepted.sec: Crop rankings of AP in India - production and productivity  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding horticulture in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Andhra Pradesh is India's largest fruit-producing State.
2. Andhra Pradesh accounts for 15.6% of India's fruit production.
3. Andhra Pradesh ranks second in mango productivity.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Andhra Pradesh is the largest fruit-producing State, contributes 15.6% of India's fruit production and ranks second in mango productivity.
accepted.tq: Check each statement against the State's overall rank, national share and crop-specific rank.
accepted.sec: Crop rankings of AP in India - production and productivity  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the position of Andhra Pradesh in oil palm cultivation?
o: It ranks first in area and second in productivity
It leads India in oil palm area, production and productivity
It leads India only in oil palm production
It ranks second in area but first in production and productivity
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh leads India in oil palm area, production and productivity. The crop is covered under the National Mission on Edible Oils–Oil Palm (NMEO-OP).
accepted.tq: Distinguish among the three separate indicators—area, production and productivity.
accepted.sec: Crop rankings of AP in India - production and productivity  [APPSC]

accepted.s: During 2023–24, which one of the following combinations relating to oil palm in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: 1.74 lakh ha, 2.27 lakh farmers, 3.10 lakh MT FFB and 17.63 lakh MT crude palm oil
2.27 lakh ha, 3.10 lakh farmers, 17.63 lakh MT FFB and 1.74 lakh MT crude palm oil
17.63 lakh ha, 1.74 lakh farmers, 2.27 lakh MT FFB and 3.10 lakh MT crude palm oil
2.27 lakh ha, 1.74 lakh farmers, 17.63 lakh MT FFB and 3.10 lakh MT crude palm oil
accepted.x: In 2023–24, oil palm covered 2.27 lakh hectares and involved 1.74 lakh farmers. Production was 17.63 lakh MT of fresh fruit bunches and 3.10 lakh MT of crude palm oil.
accepted.tq: Match the numerical indicators with their correct units and sequence.
accepted.sec: Crop rankings of AP in India - production and productivity  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the 2025–26 CDI Survey, which of the following correctly represents the additional oil palm planting and farmer coverage in Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: The 2025–26 CDI Survey reported additional planting of 22,615 hectares for 22,826 farmers.
accepted.tq: Read the paired figures carefully; APPSC commonly reverses area and beneficiary numbers.
accepted.sec: Crop rankings of AP in India - production and productivity  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following sets correctly represents the horticulture sector of Andhra Pradesh in 2024–25?
o: 18.57 lakh ha, 365.92 lakh MT production, ₹1,25,950 crore GSDP contribution and 12% growth
15.60 lakh ha, 365.92 lakh MT production, ₹1,52,950 crore GSDP contribution and 18% growth
18.23 lakh ha, 406.38 lakh MT production, ₹1,52,950 crore GSDP contribution and 21% growth
18.57 lakh ha, 406.38 lakh MT production, ₹1,52,950 crore GSDP contribution and 21% growth
accepted.x: The 2024–25 figures are 18.57 lakh hectares, 406.38 lakh MT, ₹1,52,950 crore and 21% growth. The earlier figures of 18.23 lakh hectares and 365.92 lakh MT belong to the earlier estimate.
accepted.tq: Use the year to distinguish revised current figures from earlier estimates.
accepted.sec: Crop rankings of AP in India - production and productivity  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Andhra Pradesh contributes approximately what share of India's cultured shrimp exports?
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh contributes approximately 75% of India's cultured shrimp exports. The figure of about 32% refers to its share of India's overall seafood exports.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between shrimp exports and total seafood exports.
accepted.sec: Aquaculture and fisheries - rank, exports, welfare schemes  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh's seafood exports is correct?
o: Andhra Pradesh ranked first among States in seafood export value in 2022–23.
Andhra Pradesh contributes nearly 75% of India's total seafood exports.
Andhra Pradesh's seafood export share was about 32% only in 2024–25.
Shrimp accounts for nearly 70% of Andhra Pradesh's seafood export basket.
accepted.x: Shrimp constitutes approximately 70% of Andhra Pradesh's seafood export basket. The State contributed about 32% of India's seafood exports in 2022–23 and 2023–24 and topped export value among States in 2024–25.
accepted.tq: Separate the export basket composition from the State's national export share and rank.
accepted.sec: Aquaculture and fisheries - rank, exports, welfare schemes  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In 2024–25, India's preliminary seafood export was reported as approximately:
accepted.x: India's preliminary 2024–25 seafood export was 16,98,170 MT, valued at ₹62,408.45 crore, or about US$7.45 billion.
accepted.tq: Keep physical quantity, rupee value and State-level production figures distinct.
accepted.sec: Aquaculture and fisheries - rank, exports, welfare schemes  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

List-I (Year)
A. 2023–24
B. 2024–25
C. 2025–26

List-II (Target and production in Andhra Pradesh)
i. Target 56.62 LMT; production 55.39 LMT
 ii. Target 52.55 LMT; production 51.58 LMT
 iii. Target 66.62 LMT; production 47.28 LMT up to December 2025

Codes:
accepted.x: The correct matching is 2023–24 with 52.55 and 51.58 LMT, 2024–25 with 56.62 and 55.39 LMT, and 2025–26 with 66.62 and 47.28 LMT up to December 2025.

accepted.s: The production of 47.28 lakh tonnes reported for Andhra Pradesh in 2025–26 represented approximately what percentage of the target?
accepted.x: The 47.28 lakh tonnes recorded up to December 2025 represented 72% of the 2025–26 target of 66.62 lakh tonnes.
accepted.tq: Relate the production figure to the corresponding annual target rather than to an earlier year.
accepted.sec: Aquaculture and fisheries - rank, exports, welfare schemes  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The figure of 41.38 lakh tonnes, representing 73.1% in the APSES 2024–25 reference, related to:
o: The target for fish production in 2025–26
Fish production up to December 2024, not a full-year decline
accepted.x: The figure of 41.38 lakh tonnes and 73.1% referred only to production up to December 2024. It should not be interpreted as a full-year fall in production.
accepted.tq: Use the time-period qualifier to distinguish interim production from full-year data.
accepted.sec: Aquaculture and fisheries - rank, exports, welfare schemes  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the principal export species and the related institutional activity in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Vannamei shrimp is the main export item, while black tiger shrimp brood multiplication is undertaken at the FAO centre in West Godavari
Carp is the main export item, while black tiger shrimp brood multiplication is undertaken at the MPEDA centre in Vijayawada
Vannamei shrimp is the main export item, while black tiger shrimp brood multiplication is undertaken at the MPEDA centre in Visakhapatnam
Black tiger shrimp is the main export item, while Vannamei brood multiplication is undertaken at the MPEDA centre in Kurnool
accepted.x: Vannamei, or white-leg shrimp, is the main export item. Black tiger shrimp (Penaeus monodon) brood multiplication is undertaken at the MPEDA centre at Visakhapatnam.
accepted.tq: Match the species, export role and institution–location pair without swapping them.
accepted.sec: Aquaculture and fisheries - rank, exports, welfare schemes  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about India's position in global fisheries:
1. India is the second-largest fish producer in the world.
2. India accounts for approximately 8% of world fish output.
3. India is the second-largest producer in aquaculture.
4. India leads the world in inland capture fisheries.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct in the stated national frame. India is second in fish production, contributes about 8% of world output, ranks second in aquaculture and leads in inland capture fisheries with about 2.2 MT.
accepted.tq: Check whether each statement belongs to the global production, aquaculture or inland-capture comparison.
accepted.sec: Aquaculture and fisheries - rank, exports, welfare schemes  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which district is known as the Rice Bowl of Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: East Godavari is known as the Rice Bowl of Andhra Pradesh. Its delta rice cultivation is supported by canal irrigation.
accepted.tq: Use the district–regional identity association, while avoiding confusion with horticulture and coffee regions.
accepted.sec: District-wise agriculture - rice bowl, food crops, spices, land use  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match the following crops with their principal district or region in Andhra Pradesh:

List-I (Crop)
A. Paddy
B. Groundnut
C. Tobacco
D. Coffee

List-II (District or region)
i. Anantapur
 ii. East Godavari and the Godavari–Krishna deltas
 iii. Prakasam and Guntur
 iv. Alluri Sitharama Raju district, especially Araku

Codes:
accepted.x: Paddy is concentrated in East Godavari and the Godavari–Krishna deltas; groundnut in Anantapur; tobacco in Prakasam and Guntur; and coffee in the ASR–Araku region.
accepted.tq: Start with distinctive pairs such as Anantapur–groundnut and Araku–coffee.
accepted.sec: District-wise agriculture - rice bowl, food crops, spices, land use  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following combinations is correctly matched with the crop and its major area of cultivation in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Maize — confined to the coastal delta and unrelated to poultry demand
Banana — chiefly cultivated in the Araku coffee clusters
Cotton — Rayalaseema black soils, Guntur and Kurnool
Chillies — only the Alluri Sitharama Raju district
accepted.x: Cotton is associated with the black soils of Rayalaseema and the districts of Guntur and Kurnool. Chillies are prominent in Guntur and the Krishna zone, maize in Godavari and Krishna districts, and bananas in Rayalaseema clusters.
accepted.tq: Find the correctly matched crop–region pair and reject absolute location claims.
accepted.sec: District-wise agriculture - rice bowl, food crops, spices, land use  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Rayalaseema accounts for approximately what share of Andhra Pradesh's horticulture area and output, respectively?
accepted.x: Rayalaseema is the horticulture hub of Andhra Pradesh, accounting for about 45% of horticulture area and 52% of horticulture output. It has around 19.50 lakh acres under horticulture.
accepted.tq: Do not reverse the area share and output share in a comparison question.
accepted.sec: District-wise agriculture - rice bowl, food crops, spices, land use  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the recent horticultural profile of Rayalaseema?
o: 7.8 lakh ha under horticulture and GVA of ₹7,645.8 crore
7.8 lakh ha under horticulture and GVA of ₹76,458 crore
19.50 lakh ha under horticulture and GVA of ₹76,458 crore
45 lakh ha under horticulture and GVA of ₹52,000 crore
accepted.x: Rayalaseema leads Andhra Pradesh's horticulture sector with about 7.8 lakh hectares and a gross value added of ₹76,458 crore.
accepted.tq: Separate the regional area figure from the wider horticulture-area figure for the whole State.
accepted.sec: District-wise agriculture - rice bowl, food crops, spices, land use  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Onion compensation amounting to ₹128.33 crore was provided to farmers of which districts during 2025–26?
accepted.x: During 2025–26, onion compensation of ₹128.33 crore was provided to farmers in Kurnool and YSR Kadapa districts.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact district pair attached to the compensation measure.
accepted.sec: District-wise agriculture - rice bowl, food crops, spices, land use  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The geographical area of Andhra Pradesh is approximately:
accepted.x: The geographical area of Andhra Pradesh is about 162.97 lakh hectares.
accepted.tq: Use numerical discrimination among closely similar area figures.
accepted.sec: District-wise agriculture - rice bowl, food crops, spices, land use  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In 2024–25, approximately what proportion of Andhra Pradesh's geographical area was under cultivation?
accepted.x: About 49.55 lakh hectares, or 30.4% of Andhra Pradesh's geographical area, was under cultivation in 2024–25.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the absolute cultivated area from its percentage of geographical area.
accepted.sec: District-wise agriculture - rice bowl, food crops, spices, land use  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding cropping intensity in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Cropping intensity was 1.88 in 2024–25.
2. The figure reported for 2023–24 was 1.21.
3. The two figures refer to the same agricultural year.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Cropping intensity was 1.88 in 2024–25 and 1.21 in 2023–24. Therefore, the figures do not refer to the same agricultural year.
accepted.tq: Test the year attached to each numerical figure; the false statement reverses the time distinction.
accepted.sec: District-wise agriculture - rice bowl, food crops, spices, land use  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Small and marginal farmers holding up to 2 hectares constitute approximately what share of India's farmers?
accepted.x: Farmers with holdings of up to 2 hectares constitute approximately 86.2% of India's farmers.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise percentage rather than selecting a nearby rounded figure.
accepted.sec: District-wise agriculture - rice bowl, food crops, spices, land use  [APPSC]
